messages:
jin: Heads up — CI microbench just failed on main after the merge a few minutes ago. perf-bot posted threshold diffs for batcher/kv paths. Could be a rollout blocker, flagging here :eyes:
perf-bot: AUTOMATION: microbench-suite/batcher_kv failed on main (build 741). Threshold diffs: avg latency +11.8%, p99 +13.9%, KV hitrate down 0.86 -> 0.59. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/reports/741/artifacts
sam: Link works. Quick summary from artifacts: baseline avg 2.37ms -> 2.65ms, p99 28.3ms -> 32.2ms, kv_hit 0.86->0.60. Fwiw these numbers line up with local repro I just ran against latest main.
maria: Suspect change to kernel-autoselect heuristics in commit abc123 (merged in PR 9142). That commit changed affinity scoring and added warmer warmup windows — could shift kernel choice for short sequences and reduce KV reuse.
alex: If this is real, we should hold the release. Can someone bisect to the offending commit and test revert?
jin: Assigning to @sam to bisect quickly and confirm. If confirmed, revert on main and cut a follow-up fix PR. Sam, can you run the microbench harness with the perf knobs?
sam: Starting bisect. Command I'm using:
```
# run microbench for a specific commit
python infra/perf/run_microbench.py --commit {sha} --suite batcher_kv --runs 7 --seed 42 --collect-kv-stats
```
Running abc123 now. Will post raw numbers.
sam: Results: commit abc123 shows avg 2.66ms (+12.2%), p99 32.1ms (+13.4%), kv_hit 0.60. Reverting to previous commit (def456) avg 2.37ms, p99 28.5ms, kv_hit 0.85. Reproducible across 5 runs.
maria: OK that's pretty clear. The kernel selector changed .score() weighting: it now biases shorter warmup counts which pushes short sequences to fallback kernels. That explains KV miss increase. I can make a small repro patch to toggle the weighting.
ryan: From QA perspective hold on rollout. Any customer-facing impact? Looks infra-level latency spike; no safety issues.
alex: I'll hold the rollout and open a revert. jin, do we want an immediate revert on main or a rollback branch?
jin: Revert on main and block further rollouts until we have a fix patch. Sam, please open the revert PR and link to this thread. Also include perf artifacts and the bisect log.
sam: Created revert PR: https://git.internal/redwood/repo/pull/9250 (revert commit abc123). CI for revert is running (build 742). I'll link benchmark artifacts once complete.
perf-bot: CI update: revert PR 9250 build 742: microbench-suite/batcher_kv shows avg delta -0.8% vs baseline (within noise), kv_hit 0.85 -> 0.84.
maria: Good. Next steps: I propose we pin the kernel-autoselect config behind a feature flag to test heuristics more conservatively, and add a microbench that asserts KV hitrate within tighter bounds for short-seq workloads. I'll open follow-ups: 1) feature-flag PR for selector 2) test that captures kv_hit regression 3) root-cause patch to weighting logic.
jin: Sounds good. Also add a perf test in CI to run batcher_kv on merge to main with the new kv-hit assertion so we catch regressions earlier.
alex: :thumbsup: Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. Sam — once revert passes CI, merge and schedule a small canary rollout.
sam: Revert merged, canary queued. I'll attach the bisect log here: https://ci.internal/reports/741/bisect.log
ryan: Will monitor canary dashboards for tail latency for next 2 hours and report back.
maria: I'll follow up with a PR for the fix and the feature flag. Tagging this thread in the PR description.
perf-bot: ACTIONS: revert PR 9250 merged at 2539000300, canary started, monitoring hooks enabled.
jin: Closing the loop — rollback prevented customer impact. We'll treat this a release-blocker root-cause postmortem in next all-hands. Thanks team.
